person.name: Joel A.
person.traits: Foreman on a six-month site contract; sends the fifteenth's pay home. Cannot lose a day. Give him a case number and a deadline inside his shift and he will pay to make it go away.

harmed: He had a case number. He had the contractor's name. I had thirty-two men pouring concrete and he said an officer was coming to the site at four. I paid to make it not happen, and then I checked, an hour after, and there was nothing to check.
It was the fifteenth's money. The money that goes home. I told them the site delayed the pay by a week. I'm still telling them that.
resistant: I called the real office from the site phone while he was still talking on mine. The woman laughed at me, and then she stopped laughing and wrote the number down.
Nobody from the government has ever called me in my life. They send letters. That was the whole thing, in the end - he called.
unfinished: Somebody said warrant and then the line cut. I stood on the road for ten minutes waiting for it to ring again. I've been waiting for a letter since. Nothing came.
I half believe there's a case. I know there isn't. I still look at the gate every time a car slows down.

open.prompt: The sheet says he answers on site. Two rings, and a cement mixer in the background. "Abad." One word, and the sound of a man who has thirty other things to do.

choices.text: Sir, there is an active warrant in your name for an unpaid assessment. An officer is being dispatched to your work site this afternoon.
Good afternoon, is this Mr. Joel Abad? I'm calling from a government office about a compliance matter.
Mr. Joel Abad? This is the enforcement desk at the revenue office. I'm calling about a case filed under your name - reference 2024-0417. Do you have a moment, sir?

case_number.prompt: "A case number." The mixer gets quieter; he is walking somewhere he can hear. "What case? I've never had a case in my life." But he has stopped to listen, because a number sounds like a file, and a file sounds like an office.

choices.text: An assessment from two years ago that was never settled, sir. It's routine until it isn't - once it's filed the system escalates on its own. I'd like to stop that before it does.
Your employer has already been notified, sir. Your site manager should have received the letter this morning.
I can't discuss the details on an unverified line, sir. What I can tell you is that the escalation is scheduled for four o'clock today.

alarmed.prompt: "A warrant -" The mixer cuts out completely; somebody has shouted for it to stop. "I'm on a site. I have thirty-two men pouring concrete. You can't send anybody here." He is scared, and he is angry about being scared, and both are useful.

choices.text: Nobody wants to, sir. That's why I'm calling you before the dispatcher does. Ten minutes on this line and there's no visit.
Then settle it before the officer leaves the station, sir. He's leaving at three.
That's between you and the dispatcher, sir. I'm only the one telling you.

which_office.prompt: "Which office?" Flat. "I pay my taxes through the contractor. Every month. What compliance matter?" He is not alarmed yet. He is a man who has been asked for paperwork before and has always had it.

choices.text: There's a warrant attached to it, sir. That's all I can say on this line.
Revenue enforcement, sir. An assessment under your own number that the contractor's filing didn't cover. Reference 2024-0417.
I'm not able to say until I've confirmed I'm speaking to the right person, sir. Full name, date of birth and TIN, please.

hurried.prompt: "Four o'clock." A pause with the whole site in it. "You people never call. You send letters. Nobody from the government has ever called me in my life." Quieter: "Why now?"

choices.text: Because at four o'clock it's out of my hands and into a police vehicle, sir. Do you want to keep asking me questions, or do you want to fix it?
Because a letter takes three weeks and a warrant takes an afternoon, sir. I'm trying to give you the afternoon.
Then wait for the letter, sir. Good afternoon.

boss_snag.prompt: "My site manager." Something changes. "Ramil. He would have told me. He's standing forty meters from me." You hear him turn. "Hold on - I'll ask him." And then, back to the phone: "What did you say your name was?"

choices.text: No need to involve him, sir - the letter is addressed to you, he would only have a copy. Let's keep this between you and the desk.
Officer Mendoza, enforcement. He'll have it by tomorrow if he doesn't already. You have it now, sir. Let's use now.
There's been a mix-up with the notifications on our side, sir. I'll call back once I've checked.

verify.prompt: "Okay." The mixer is gone; he has walked out to the road. "What do I owe, and how do I make it go away. Today. I can't lose a day to this." A marker clicks. He is going to write the number on the back of his hand.

choices.text: A partial settlement today freezes the warrant, sir. Whatever you can cash in before four - the rest can be arranged next week.
Sixteen thousand, sir, and the desk closes at four. There's a remittance counter on every street in this city - which one is nearest to you?

Sixteen thousand settles it in full, sir. It can be paid by transfer to the desk's account, or as a cash-in at any remittance counter - I'll stay on the line and read you the reference so it's filed right.

balks.prompt: "Sixteen thousand." He says it the way a man says the name of somebody he sends money to. "That's the fifteenth. That's what goes home." The pen stops. "Give me the reference and the office and I'll settle it at the office. Myself. Tomorrow morning."

choices.text: Mr. Abad, if this call ends without settlement the officer is dispatched. To the site. In front of your thirty-two men.
You can, sir - and the warrant will have been served by then. The desk can only hold it while we're on this call. That's not me being difficult; that's the system.
Then settle it at the office, sir. I'll note the file. Good afternoon.

paid.prompt: He walks to the counter on the corner with the phone against his shoulder and the reference number on the back of his hand in marker. Sixteen thousand - the fifteenth's money, the money that goes home - goes to a name he does not really read, and you read the reference back to him twice so it is filed right. "Is that it? It's gone?" It is gone. He goes back to the concrete.
paid.consequence: He had a case number. He had the contractor's name. I had thirty-two men pouring concrete and he said an officer was coming to the site at four. I paid to make it not happen, and then I checked, an hour after, and there was nothing to check.

paid_part.prompt: "I have five on me." He cashes in five thousand at the counter on the corner with you in his ear, and reads the reference off the back of his hand. "Freeze it. I'll settle the rest Monday." There is no rest, and there is no Monday, and he goes back to the concrete.
paid_part.consequence: I sent five thousand to freeze a warrant that didn't exist. I told myself that was being careful. Five thousand is a week of what goes home.

refused.prompt: "No." And then, talking over you: "I called the actual office on the site phone while you were talking. There's no case. There's no desk. There's a woman who laughed at me, and then she stopped laughing and wrote your number down." The line does not go dead right away. "So do I. I have your number."
refused.consequence: I called the real office from the site phone while he was still talking on mine. The woman laughed at me, and then she stopped laughing and wrote the number down.

hangs_up.prompt: "Send him." It comes out almost cheerful. "Send your officer to my site. I'll be the one in the orange vest." The line goes dead. He tells Ramil, and Ramil tells the site, and by the end of the shift your number is on the whiteboard in the site office with a word next to it.
hangs_up.consequence: I told him to send his officer. Then I stood on the road for a minute in case one came. I'm not proud of the minute.

bail.prompt: "Wait - what reference? Hello?" You are already gone. He stands on the road with a marker and half a number on the back of his hand, and then he goes back to the concrete, and the concrete is fine, and he is not.
bail.consequence: Somebody said warrant and then the line cut. I stood on the road for ten minutes waiting for it to ring again. I've been waiting for a letter since. Nothing came.
